subject: Renewal & capacity uplift: proposal and MAP
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@swiftcart.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30 14:12 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation: commit flexibility & uplift

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the intro earlier this month. SwiftCart has seen a meaningful uptick in inference demand tied to our holiday push — Q3 overage is +42% vs plan. We want to lock pricing for the next 12 months but also need flexibility to scale capacity quickly.

Procurement is starting budget reviews next week. Two asks from my side: 1) can you outline a renewal option that includes a temporary price hold while we ramp, and 2) a one-time credit or amortized rebate to cover Q3 overage? I attached Q3 usage for context.

Would be great to get an initial economics sketch before we go to PO.

Thanks,
Tom Li
Head of Platform
SwiftCart

Attachment: SwiftCart_Q3_usage_report.pdf (pdf, 420KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@swiftcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01 09:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: commit flexibility & uplift

Tom —

Appreciate the usage file. Quick readback / options we can put on the table to keep you covered during the holiday spike while giving you predictable cost: 

- Option A (Short price-hold + credit): 12-month renewal at an 18% list discount, plus a 3-month price hold that freezes per-token pricing at current effective rate. One-time operational credit of $50,000 to offset Q3 overage applied to the first invoice.
- Option B (Commit conversion + staggered credits): Convert 50% of your current retainer to a committed throughput unit (CTU) with a 12-month term at 20% discount; remaining consumption on pay-as-you-go with a tiered overage credit schedule (up to 40% credit for overages caused by holiday-driven uplift, subject to caps).
- Option C (Burst pool & staircase uplift): Keep current retainer, add a 6-month burst pool with guaranteed capacity and a smaller uplift discount (15%), plus an SLA uplift for guaranteed burst activation times.

I've attached a draft amendment (Proposed_AMENDMENT_v2.pdf) and an SLA table for the burst model. From an approval perspective, I need internal sign-off on the $50k credit and the temporary price-hold. Can you confirm procurement timing and whether you prefer one consolidated amendment or a short-term addendum + longer-term master amendment?

If you like, let's book a 30-minute call this week to walk through numbers and MAP (mutual action plan).

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Exec — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Proposed_AMENDMENT_v2.pdf, SLA_Tier_Table.xlsx

From: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@swiftcart.com>

Date: 2026-10-02 10:21 -0700

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the quick options. A few clarifying questions before we sync:

- For Option A, is the $50k credit one-off or spread over invoices? How does that appear on the first two invoices?
- For Option B, can you show an example invoice comparing today vs. committed pricing with our Q3 usage profile? Procurement wants line-item visibility.
- For all options: can the price hold be limited to specific model families / routes? We only need the hold for generation-heavy routes that power recommendations.

Procurement would prefer a single consolidated amendment (amend + exhibit) to avoid separate addenda. Our PO cycle closes 10/18; we need a signed amendment by 10/15 to land a Nov 1 renewal effective date.

Also please include a short MAP with milestones (signature, PO, migration window, billing start). Can you flag any operational constraints if we convert retainer -> CTUs?

Thanks,
Ana Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager
SwiftCart

Adding ops color — David ran a quick feasibility check on converting 50% of the retainer to CTUs. Key notes: 

> From: David Kim
> - Converting retainer -> CTU is straightforward; we map historical token velocity to baseline CTU sizing. There is one caveat: KV cache hit behavior on recommendation routes changes cost profile, so we should scope which routes get committed pricing.
> - Burst pool: we can provision a 6-month burst pool with cold start guarantees if the customer accepts a 2x activation window for the first 48 hours.
> - Overage credits require a one-time operational reconciliation (usage audit) and are capped to avoid adverse selection.

Suggested operational guardrails to include in the amendment: route-level scoping for price-hold, a one-time usage reconciliation for the $50k credit, and a capped overage credit ladder that phases down after the holiday window.

I've attached the SLA_Tier_Table.xlsx as an example of the burst service levels. If SwiftCart confirms route scoping, we can produce a committed pricing appendix showing CTU sizing and expected spend.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final proposal & next steps (MAP + signature link)

Tom / Ana —

Thanks for the quick turn. To keep procurement on track, here is a prioritized, executable proposal and MAP: 

Executive economics (if you want a single line):
- 12-month term, consolidated amendment (preferred by SwiftCart).
- Agreed: 18% list discount on the committed portion.
- Price hold: 3 months on scoped generation routes (applies to model families: gen-v1, gen-v2).
- One-time credit: $50,000 applied to first invoice (one-off; shows as line item "Q3 Overage Credit").
- Commit conversion: convert 50% of current retainer to CTUs (seed CTU sizing attached).

Operational MAP (dates are targetable to meet your 10/15 sign timeline):
- 10/06: Redwood sends amended agreement + committed pricing appendix (you review).
- 10/08: Joint pricing call to walk CTU examples and route scoping (30m).
- 10/11: Procurement submits PO to Redwood.
- 10/15: Signed amendment executed (DocuSign link below).
- 11/01: New term & billing effective date.

Links & docs:
- Amendment (draft) — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/67890/deal/DEAL-4521
- DocuSign (draft) — https://www.docusign.com/recipient/abc123-SWC-4521-amendment

If you approve Option A today, I have approval to submit the amendment for signature with the $50k credit.

Thanks — happy to join a call as needed.
